course_name_en: Principles and Institutions of Democratic Culture

learning_outcomes.text: Students will better understand the philosophical foundations of democracy.
Students will be able to explain the conceptual framework, institutions, and procedures of a functioning democracy, along with its limitations.
Students will be able to critically evaluate daily life and political practices in light of democratic ideals.
Students will develop skills to participate in social and political life with their own thoughts and preferences as active citizens.
Students will be able to perform analyses regarding the future of democracy in the age of globalization.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the Course: Definitions of Democracy
Philosophical and Moral Foundations of Democracy
Democracy and Ideologies: Types of Democracy: Liberal and Social Democracy Models
Democracy and Law: Constitutional Democracy, Rule of Law, and Separation of Powers
Democracy and Political Institutions: Parliament, Political Parties, and Electoral Systems
Democracy and Pluralism: Majority Rule, Minority Rights
Turkish Democracy I: From its Beginning to the Multi-party System
Turkish Democracy II: Multi-party Period: Efforts for Democratization and Interventions: Examples of Military Interventions and Political Party Closures
New Democracy Perspectives in the Global Age
bibliography: Demokrasi ve Eleştirleri, Robert A. Dahl
Liberalizm Demokrasi ve Türkiye Modeli, Prof. Dr.Mustafa Erdoğan
